mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects a restrictive monetary policy that increases the cost of capital and reduces corporate investment.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 4.5%, it indicates a failure of monetary policy to contain inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased real rate uncertainty.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change > 3.0% and FEDFUNDS <= 4.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (characterized by high housing starts), a monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 0.5% signals an impending economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST declines > 0.5% in a late-cycle expansion regime over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals a weakening manufacturing sector that reduces corporate profits, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) combined with a decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a shift in consumer spending away from durable goods (housing) toward services, which is a sign of economic fragility and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 2.0% and HOUST monthly change < -0.5%
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS monthly change > 2.0% and HOUST monthly change < -0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals a strengthening manufacturing sector that boosts corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO increases > 0.5% over any 3-year rolling window.
